name: Sumatriptan
summary: The prototypical triptan: a selective 5-HT1B/1D agonist that aborts migraine attacks and cluster headache, with subcutaneous injection as the fastest, most reliable route.
mechanism: Selective agonist at 5-HT1B/1D receptors — constricts dilated cranial vessels and inhibits trigeminal nociceptive transmission.

dosing.adult: 50–100 mg PO at onset, repeat after 2 h if needed; SC 6 mg (may repeat once after 1 h)

safety.pregnancy: Limited data; no clear major teratogenicity — use the lowest effective frequency
contraindications: Ischemic heart disease or coronary vasospasm (including Prinzmetal angina)
Ergotamines or other triptans within 24 h
warnings: Coronary vasospasm/ischemia — assess cardiovascular risk before first use
Serotonin syndrome when combined with SSRIs/SNRIs/MAOIs
Chest pressure or tightness is common — usually benign but requires evaluation
Medication-overuse headache if used more than ~2 days/week
monitoring: Cardiovascular risk assessment before first dose
safety.overdose: Hypertension, chest symptoms; mostly benign, supportive care

indications: Acute migraine with or without aura
clinicalPearls: Efficacy is best when taken early — at the first sign of migraine, before the attack peaks
SC gives the fastest, most reliable relief and is the standard for cluster headache; chest tightness is usually benign but must be evaluated in patients with cardiac risk
good: Acute migraine attacks — especially the SC form for cluster headache — when cardiovascular risk is low.
bad: Patients with coronary disease, uncontrolled hypertension, or attacks more than ~2 days/week (overuse headache).

provenance.notes: Curated from standard neurology/pharmacology references. Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
